text:
Alex: Heads up — I'm seeing KV cache reuse drop ~40% for a subset of requests when clients switch conversation_id mid-stream. Repro on staging and a small slice in prod. :eyes:
Marta: Which key format are we using for those prefixes? is conversation_id part of the cache key?
Alex: Yeah, current key is basically: `sha(tenant + '::' + conversation_id + '::' + prefix)`
Alex: Example eviction log snippet (from staging):
```
[2026-03-10T18:12:02Z] tenant=acme reuse_rate=0.12 evictions=23 mem_used=7.8Gi
[2026-03-10T18:12:05Z] evict key=sha(....) reason=low_access_window
```
Chen: My hunch: conversation_id is noisy (users create ephemeral conv ids or clients URL-encode differently). That amplifies fragmentation across shards and prevents cross-request reuse.
Chen: Two quick ideas: normalize conversation_id (strip whitespace, normalize case, decode percent-escapes) OR drop conv_id from key for short prefixes and rely on tenant+prefix only.
Sam: Dropping conv_id risks leaking KV across logical sessions for same tenant. Could be fine for prefix-level cache (non-sensitive) but we should be explicit. Another option: add a sticky-hint header so upstream can opt-in to keep the same session routing (helps reuse without changing keying).
Marta: Can we measure impact without a full rollout? small canary: 5% traffic with `X-Cache-Sticky: prefer` + normalizer middleware.
Alex: Ran that 5% canary for 20m: reuse_rate jumped from 0.12 -> 0.62, evictions/sec fell ~3.6x. Quick raw from /internal/cache/stats?tenant=acme
```
canary=false reuse_rate=0.12 evictions_per_min=138 mem=7.8Gi
canary=true  reuse_rate=0.62 evictions_per_min=38  mem=7.6Gi
```
Alex: So sticky routing + lightweight normalization looks promising.
Chen: Nice. Two followups: 1) add deterministic key normalizer function (`normalize_conv_id`) and run unit+property tests to ensure idempotence; 2) experiment with TTL tiers: keep conv-scoped entries short, global prefix entries longer.
Sam: Also watch shard hotness sizes — sticky routing concentrates load and could bump kernel scheduling on some GPUs. We may need to floor per-shard batch sizes or bias routing for load leveling.
Marta: Proposed rollout plan:
- implement `normalize_conv_id` in runtime keying layer (fail closed)
- add opt-in `X-Cache-Sticky` header handling (config flag default off)
- K8s canary: 5% -> 20% -> 100% if metrics look good
- add telemetry: reuse_rate, evictions, shard_load, mem_growth per-tenant
Marta: I'll open a PR and a short RFC with benchmarks. :thumbsup:
Alex: Thanks — I'll attach sample traces and add the staging run to the RFC.
infra-bot: deploy/cluster-canary started by Marta on cluster=staging (canary=5%)
Sam: Quick note — when you add the telemetry, include per-seq-len breakdowns. long-contexts show different mem-growth patterns.
Alex: Will do.
Marta: Great, assigning tasks in the RFC.
